data.text:
The No-Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP) will continue despite suspension of EDSA rehabilitation, the Department of Transportation and the MMDA said.

“NCAP is not just about EDSA… it’s about a more efficient way of enforcing our traffic rules,” says Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon.

Meanwhile, MMDA Head of Special Operations Gabriel Go says there is no reason to stop the enforcement of NCAP, especially since traffic is visibly more orderly now. | via @andietagz & @JervisManahan

Transport groups staged a protest caravan from the University of the Philippines (UP) Diliman to the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) main office in Pasig on Monday, June 2, to oppose the implementation of the No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP).
